Content:
Suppose we want to find all of the values of [MATH: x] that satisfy either [MATH: 4x+2 < 6] or [MATH: 2x \geq 8.]

Content:
To do this, we solve each inequality individually and then compute the union of the two solutions.

Content:
We start by solving [MATH: 4x+2 < 6\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: 4x + 2|< 6; 4x|< 4; x|< 1]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/52952fcc9431374e3b2f7dab2804a802]

Content:
Then, we solve [MATH: 2x \geq 8\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: 2x|≥ 8; x|≥ 4]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/84a736826d245d96a936fe7f05039190]

Content:
To graph the values of [MATH: x] that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/109fce543e939c85d2abcc472e3df7bb]

Content:
Thus, the final solution is [MATH: x < 1] or [MATH: x \geq 4.] We can write this using interval notation as

Content:
[MATH: (-\infty, 1) \cup [4,\infty).]
